_comment: One record per edition PAGE. Two extensions ship today, so two distinct storeUrls: the YouTube listing also covers Netflix (one install, both sites — see its manifest matches), which is why the netflix record points at the same URL and says so. Adding a record here creates the card on the home page and the /<slug>/ landing page. storeUrl empty renders a disabled '#' link.

editions.name: Lingogram for YouTube
editions.card: Fills the missing second track with YouTube's auto-translation.
editions.sub: Your target language and your own together on any YouTube video that has captions — including auto-generated ones. Tap a word to keep it in your personal dictionary.

points.d: Works with every caption track, including YouTube's auto-generated ones.
If one of your two languages isn't there, Lingogram fills it with YouTube's automatic translation, so you always get the dual view.
The floating overlay keeps both subtitle lines on screen in fullscreen and theater mode.

faq.q: Does it work with auto-generated captions?
faq.a: Yes — any caption track works, including auto-generated ones.

faq.q: What if the video has captions in only one language?
faq.a: Lingogram fills the second track with YouTube's automatic translation. Automatic translations aren't perfect, but they keep you moving.

editions.name: Lingogram for Netflix
editions.card: Original subtitle tracks, no machine translation.
editions.sub: Lingogram pairs the subtitle tracks a title actually has — the original plus a translation — and shows them side by side. No machine translation, ever.

points.d: Only the tracks the title actually carries — human-made subtitles, not machine output.
Pick which available languages play as primary and secondary, and swap them with one shortcut.
Lingogram turns Netflix's own captions off while the overlay is on, so lines never stack.

faq.a: No. Lingogram for Netflix only shows the subtitle tracks a title actually has. When a title carries tracks in both of your languages, you get the dual view.

faq.q: Which titles does it work on?
faq.a: Any title with subtitles. The dual view appears when the title offers tracks in both of your languages.

editions.name: Lingogram for HDrezka
editions.card: Dual tracks when a title carries them.
editions.sub: The interactive transcript, listening challenge and one-tap word saving work on any HDrezka title with a subtitle track. When a title carries two tracks — the original plus a translation — you get dual subtitles.

points.d: Most HDrezka titles carry a single subtitle track — usually English — and that alone powers the transcript, listening challenge and word saving.
When a title also offers a second language (English plus Russian, for example), Lingogram shows both as dual subtitles. No machine translation — only the tracks a title actually has.
The floating overlay keeps your subtitles on screen, fullscreen included.

faq.a: No. Lingogram only ever shows the subtitle tracks a title actually has. Dual subtitles appear on titles that carry two tracks.

faq.q: Which titles does it work on?
faq.a: Any HDrezka title that has a subtitle track — switch the audio to the original and turn its subtitles on.
